title: Pocari Sweat Run Bandung 2026 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Pocari Sweat Run Bandung 2026 Review: Route, Cut-offs, Traffic
meta_description: Pocari Sweat Run Bandung 2026 review: 8,400 half marathoners on a 21.3 km city tour from Balai Kota, 4am waves, a 13.8 km cut-off, roads shared with traffic, and how 2026 compared with 2024.
dek: What Bandung's big two-day race was like on 19 and 20 September 2026: the half-marathon tour of the city, the pre-dawn start waves and cut-offs, how the shared roads worked this time, who won, and the logistics of entering.
verdict: Enter if you want a big city half marathon or 10 km in cool pre-dawn air and can hold a steady pace. The 2026 race sent 8,400 runners on a 21.3 km tour of central Bandung on the Sunday and 7,600 round a 10.2 km loop on the Saturday, all from Balai Kota. The catch is the roads and the clock. Roads are diverted and shared rather than closed, and in 2024 runners fought motorbikes and cars; 2026 went far more smoothly. The last half-marathon wave had to reach 13.8 km in 2 hours 30 and finish in 3 hours 30. Know the cut-off, and expect vehicles at junctions.

sections.heading: The Course: A Tour of Central Bandung From City Hall
paragraphs: Both races started and finished at Balai Kota, Bandung's city hall, by Taman Vanda on Jl. Merdeka [1][2]. The half marathon runs along Jl. Ir H Juanda to a U-turn near St Borromeus hospital, then on through Dago and Diponegoro, Supratman, A Yani, Ibrahim Adjie and Kiaracondong to Gatot Subroto. It comes back along Asia Afrika and Jenderal Sudirman, then through Gardujati, Pasir Kaliki, HOS Cokroaminoto and Pajajaran, and back via Cicendo, Wastukencana and Merdeka to the finish [1]. Local press gave its length as 21.3 km, and the 10 km's as 10.2 km [3].

The 10 km route the organiser posted on the Thursday before the race runs from Taman Vanda along Wastukencana and Ir H Juanda to the same U-turn near St Borromeus, then through Dago, Diponegoro, Cilamaya, RE Martadinata (Riau), Aceh and Belitung to Jl. Merdeka [3]. An earlier published version had a U-turn on Teuku Umar and a loop via Kalimantan and Sumatra streets [1].
One runner's favourite stretch of the half marathon was the Kiaracondong flyover at sunrise, running above the station sign below [4].

sections.heading: The Weather: Cool Before Dawn
paragraphs: There are no airport weather observations to report for race morning: the public METAR archive has no records for Bandung's Husein Sastranegara airport for September 2026 [5].

Runners' accounts point to cool conditions. A Jakarta runner who has done the race several times said the 4am start meant it was cool at the start and cool at the finish [4]. In 2024, too, runners singled out the cool air as the race's strength [6].

sections.heading: Start Waves and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The half marathon on Sunday started in three waves, at 4.00, 4.07 and 4.15am; bag drop and the runners' entrance opened at 2.30am and the start corrals at 3am [7]. The 10 km on Saturday was planned for waves at 4.45, 4.52 and 5.00am, with bag drop from 3.15am [7]; the flag-offs were reported to run from about 4.50am to about 5.20am [8].

The half marathon had a cut-off point at 13.8 km at 6.45am and a finish cut-off at 7.45am; the 10 km closed at 7am [7]. For the last wave that meant 2 hours 30 minutes to reach 13.8 km, about 10:50 per km, and 3 hours 30 minutes to finish; the first wave had 15 minutes more. When entries opened in February the check was set at 14 km at 7am, and the organiser said runners who missed it would be taken to the finish by shuttle bus [9].

sections.heading: The Roads: Shared, Not Closed
paragraphs: Bandung does not close the roads for this race. Mayor Muhammad Farhan said there would be no full closures at all, only diversions and shared road space, with police in charge of traffic; the police had said that at a red light everyone stops [1][10]. Police used stop-go control along the route [10][2], and the organiser's marshals worked alongside police, the army, the transport agency and Satpol PP, which also patrolled the cheering points where running communities gather [2].

That arrangement has a history. In 2024, when the race started at Gedung Sate, half marathoners and marathoners had to contend with motorbikes and cars and constant horns, and at some points runners were made to stop and give way [6]. In 2025 the race caused congestion across the city, and it was split over two days to spread the load [11]. The mayor said the city had learned from protests over closed roads in the previous edition [10].

In 2026 it went more smoothly. After the Saturday 10 km the mayor said there had been very little horn-blowing and no traffic accidents after the start; a collision between an angkot minibus and a truck in Dago happened about five minutes before it. Traffic was held for no more than about three minutes at a time and was back to normal by 6.30am, except near the finish [12][13]. The city reported nothing untoward on the Sunday, and a runner who had done the race in earlier years said runners and vehicles competed for road space least of all this time [4].
Expect vehicles beside you and at junctions, follow the marshals, and do not assume a junction is held for you.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Robi Syianturi won the men's half marathon, from Timotius Siahaan and Arif Hidayatullah, and Nefriana Ariance Daik won the women's, from Agustina Mardika Manik and Westi Indah [14]. The 10 km on Saturday went to Rikky Marthin Luther Simbolon, from Iqbal Saputra and Nofeldi Petingko, and to Agustina Mardika Manik, who ran both days [14]. No winning times have been published.

The front of the field overlaps with Indonesia's other big weekend races: a runner named Iqbal Saputra, second in the 10 km here on Saturday, won the Garmin Run Indonesia 10 km in BSD the next morning in 32:06 [15].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Entry cost Rp650,000 for the 10 km and Rp850,000 for the half marathon, plus the ticketing platform's fee. Entries were sold only through Blibli, one ticket per account [9]. The organiser said in January that Bandung tickets usually sell out very quickly because of limited capacity, and that about 70% of runners come from outside the city [16].

The minimum age is 15 for the 10 km and 17 for the half marathon, and runners aged 15 to 17 need a letter signed by a parent or guardian [9]. Entrants get a bib, race jersey, sports insurance and a tote bag of sponsor products; finishers inside the limit get a medal, and half-marathon finishers an extra finisher jersey [9]. Race packs were collected from Thursday to Saturday, 17 to 19 September [17].

The 10 km and the half marathon are on separate days, Saturday and Sunday, and tickets were sold separately for each day [7]. The 2026 race was part of the city's 216th anniversary celebrations [14], and the organiser said it would probably stay at half-marathon distance for now rather than add a marathon, because a longer route would disrupt more of the city [12][13].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a big, well-supported city half marathon or 10 km, a pre-dawn start that runners describe as cool, and a route that tours central Bandung. It suits runners who can hold about 10 minutes per km or better through 13.8 km.
Think twice if you want closed roads, a full marathon, or a slow walk-run half: the cut-off point is strict, and the roads are shared with traffic.

The 2027 dates, fees and routes had not been published when this was written. Watch for the organiser's route update in race week; in 2026 the 10 km route changed from the version first published [1][3].

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's statements and race-week schedule as reported, local reporting in Indonesian on the 2024, 2025 and 2026 races, city officials' post-race statements, and runners' comments to the city's press office.

faqs.question: Are the 10 km and half marathon at Pocari Sweat Run Bandung on the same day?
faqs.answer: No. In 2026 the 10 km was on Saturday 19 September, with 7,600 runners, and the half marathon on Sunday 20 September, with 8,400. Both started and finished at Balai Kota, Bandung's city hall. Tickets were sold separately for each day, and the fields never share the road.

faqs.question: What are the cut-offs at Pocari Sweat Run Bandung?
faqs.answer: Strict for the half marathon. In 2026 runners had to pass 13.8 km by 6.45am and finish by 7.45am; the last wave started at 4.15am, so it had 2 hours 30 minutes to the checkpoint. The 10 km closed at 7am. The February plan had the check at 14 km by 7am.

faqs.question: Are the roads closed for Pocari Sweat Run Bandung?
faqs.answer: Not fully. In 2026 the city said there were no full closures, only diversions, stop-go control and shared road space, with police in charge. The mayor said traffic was held for up to about three minutes at a time. In 2024 runners complained of fighting motorbikes and cars; 2026 was much calmer.

faqs.question: How much does Pocari Sweat Run Bandung cost?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the 10 km cost Rp650,000 and the half marathon Rp850,000, plus the ticketing platform's fee. Tickets were sold only through Blibli, one per account. Entry included a bib, race jersey, sports insurance and sponsor products; half-marathon finishers also got an extra finisher jersey.

faqs.question: What was the weather like at Pocari Sweat Run Bandung?
faqs.answer: No airport weather record exists for race morning, because Bandung's Husein Sastranegara airport has no observations in the public archive for September 2026. Runners described the 4am half-marathon start as cool at both start and finish, and runners in 2024 also praised the cool air.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 about the 2026 edition: 10 km on Saturday 19 September, half marathon on Sunday 20 September 2026. Replaces an earlier version based on two post-race reports. No official race-information website was found; race-week details come from the organiser's Instagram as reported by Tirto, PRFM and Kompas. Where the February plan and the race-week schedule differ (cut-off point, waves), the race-week schedule is used. The organiser's updated 10 km route differs from an earlier published one; the later version is given. No weather figures: the METAR archive has no Bandung observations. Podium names were published but no times, and no public results were found. Runner comments come via the city's press office. No rating.
